patients.summary: Accountant in his early thirties who joined healthy in 2023, was found to have hypertension and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in late 2024, had a pit viper bite on a hiking trip in 2025, and was admitted to an ICU with anti-GBM (Goodpasture) disease in April 2026, now on a prednisone taper after plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 31 y/o man looking to set up primary care here. Says he hasn't had a regular doctor since finishing grad school, only the campus clinic. Works in accounting now, employer plan. Explained membership model and that labs/imaging still go through his insurance. Booked new patient physical 9/12 at 8:40. Asked him to request records from the student health service; release form emailed.

social.value: Social drinker, 2 to 4 drinks per week

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M establishing care. Last routine care through a university student clinic during his graduate program; now working as an accountant. No ongoing complaints. No chronic conditions, takes nothing regularly, no supplements. No surgeries. NKDA.

Family: father has autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. A paternal uncle died after a ruptured brain aneurysm. Mother has high blood pressure.

Social: lives alone in Easthampton. Never smoked. Drinks socially, 2-4 a week. No drug use. Runs and hikes on weekends.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: well-appearing, in no distress. Vitals per flowsheet, BP in normal range. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without concerning lesions. Extremities warm, no edema. Mood and affect normal.

Assessment/plan:
- Health maintenance, adult male. Fasting lipids, CMP. HIV and hep C screening once, he agrees. Tdap today (last tetanus shot he can recall was in high school). Flu vaccine today. PHQ-2 0.
- Family history of PKD in father noted.
- Return yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Miles, your bloodwork came back fine: LDL cholesterol just above the lab's cutoff, which at your age and with no other risk factors needs nothing but a recheck in a few years, kidney and liver function normal, blood sugar normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to have you with us.

documents.title: Student health service records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from the university student health service, covering 2018 to 2022. Contents: intake forms, two sports-type physicals with normal exams, one visit for a sprained wrist with no fracture, routine immunization history (childhood series, meningococcal and HPV series completed). No medications, no allergies listed. Scanned to chart; PCP to review.

I've been getting mild headaches on and off for a few months, figured it was screens at work. Is this something I should come in for? I missed my physical in September.

documents.author: PCP

Any chest pain, shortness of breath, vision trouble, or a sudden severe headache, go to the ED. Otherwise front desk will reach out for a visit this week.

orders.reason: Bilateral flank masses, new hypertension, father with polycystic kidney disease

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in after two pharmacy readings near 160/100. Has had mild, dull headaches a few times a week for a few months, nothing sudden or severe, no neuro symptoms. No chest pain, no change in vision, no shortness of breath. Appetite fine. Urinating normally, hasn't seen blood or dark urine. Mentions that both sides of his belly sometimes feel full, no pain. Drinks a few beers a week. No NSAID use to speak of, no decongestants, no energy drinks.

FH again: father with polycystic kidneys (on his mind, he knows it runs in families), paternal uncle died of a ruptured aneurysm, mother on BP medication.

O: BP 162/100 L arm seated, repeat after 5 min similar. HR 76. Well appearing. Fundi not well seen, no obvious abnormality. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: smooth, nontender, fullness palpable in both flanks consistent with enlarged kidneys. No edema.

A/P:
1. Hypertension, stage 2 range, young, with family history of PKD and palpable kidneys. Most likely the kidneys are the story. Start lisinopril 10 mg daily. BMP and UA today. Low-salt diet reviewed. He'd already been thinking of cutting back on drinking and says he'll just stop for now. Get a home cuff and send readings.
2. Bilateral flank masses + FH of ADPKD: referring to nephrology for evaluation and imaging; easier for them to order the ultrasound and see him with it.
3. Headaches: likely pressure-related; red flags reviewed.
RN call in 2 weeks re tolerance; recheck BMP at nephrology or here in 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: BMP and urine results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function, sodium and potassium all normal. Urine without protein or blood. Good baseline before the lisinopril settles in. Nephrology referral has been sent; their office will call you.

documents.title: BP medication check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in two weeks into lisinopril. No cough, no lightheadedness, no lip or tongue swelling. Bought a home cuff; readings still above goal so far, still early. Has stopped drinking. Nephrology appt is 12/5. Told him to bring the cuff log there and send it to us too.

events.reason: Hypertension, bilateral flank masses, family history of polycystic kidney disease

conditions.label: Chronic kidney disease, stage 1
conditions.note: Structural kidney disease from ADPKD with normal filtration

reports.text:
Indication: hypertension, palpable flank masses, father with ADPKD.
Technique: grayscale and color images of both kidneys and the bladder.
Right kidney: enlarged, 16.4 cm in length, with multiple simple-appearing cysts of varying size throughout the cortex and medulla. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing stones.
Left kidney: enlarged, 17.0 cm in length, with multiple cysts of varying size throughout. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing stones.
Normal flow in both kidneys on color imaging.
Bladder: unremarkable.
Visualized liver and spleen: unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts, consistent with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in this clinical setting. No hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group
Date of visit: 12/05/2024
Reason for consultation: elevated blood pressure, palpable flanks, family history of PKD.

Thank you for asking us to see this 32-year-old accountant. He came to attention after high readings on a pharmacy machine. For the last few months he has had mild headaches. Otherwise he feels well. He has had no chest pain, visual symptoms or breathlessness. Appetite is normal and he has noticed nothing different about his urine. He describes an occasional sense of fullness across both sides of the abdomen.

PMH: hypertension, diagnosed by his PCP last month. No prior kidney evaluation.
PSH: none.
Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily (started 11/7/24).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with ADPKD; paternal uncle with a ruptured intracranial aneurysm; mother with hypertension.
Social: accountant. Never smoker. Currently not drinking.

Exam: BP 165/102, pulse 78. Cardiac exam normal, lungs clear. Abdomen: bilateral, non-tender flank masses, smooth. No edema.

Data: serum creatinine today within normal limits; potassium normal.
Renal ultrasound performed in our office today: both kidneys enlarged (R 16.4 cm, L 17.0 cm) and replaced by numerous cysts bilaterally, no hydronephrosis or stones.

Impression:
1. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, by imaging criteria with a positive family history.
2. CKD stage 1 related to ADPKD; filtration currently preserved.
3. Hypertension secondary to ADPKD. Pressure remains high but he is only four weeks into the ACE inhibitor.

Recommendations:
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Sodium under 2 g/day; generous water intake through the day.
- Avoid NSAIDs.
- Keep a home BP log.
- With his uncle's aneurysm rupture, his own ADPKD and the recent headaches, we are arranging a screening MRI brain with non-contrast MR angiography.
- Follow up here in 6 months with BMP and urine albumin/creatinine.

Allergies: NKDA. We appreciate the referral.

documents.title: Kidney specialist visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Miles, I got the nephrology letter. As you heard from them, the ultrasound shows polycystic kidney disease, the same condition as your dad. Your kidney function is normal right now, which is the important part, and blood pressure control is the biggest thing we can do to protect it. Stick with the lisinopril, the salt and water advice, and avoid ibuprofen/naproxen type painkillers (Tylenol is fine). They're also setting up a brain MRA because of your uncle's history; that's a standard screening step. Let's do a BP visit here in about 2 months. Happy to talk anytime.

documents.title: RE: Kidney specialist visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Not a huge surprise given my dad. MRI is booked for January. Will book the follow up.

events.reason: Aneurysm screening, ADPKD with family history of aneurysm rupture

reports.text:
Outside imaging center.
Exam: MRI brain without contrast with 3D time-of-flight MR angiography of the head.
Clinical history: 33-year-old man. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease; relative with ruptured intracranial aneurysm. Screening.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Brain parenchyma normal in signal and volume. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No mass or extra-axial collection. Normal flow voids.
MRA: The intracranial internal carotid arteries, anterior, middle and posterior cerebral arteries, vertebral and basilar arteries are patent with normal caliber. Complete circle of Willis. No aneurysm identified. No stenosis or vascular malformation.
reports.conclusion: Normal MRI brain. No intracranial aneurysm on MR angiography.

BP 136/86 here, other vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

- ADPKD / CKD 1: BMP today. Nephrology f/u in June. Reminded no NSAIDs.

Outside nephrology group, follow-up visit 06/10/2025.

Miles returns six months after his ADPKD diagnosis. He has been diligent with the low-salt plan and fluids. No flank pain, no visible blood in the urine, no urinary infections. Headaches have resolved. His screening MRA in January showed no aneurysm.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

BP 134/84 in clinic.

Assessment: ADPKD with preserved kidney function, CKD stage 1. Blood pressure improved on lisinopril.
Plan: continue current regimen. Repeat labs and visit in 6 months. Avoid NSAIDs.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, regional medical center (North Carolina)
Date of service: 08/08/2025, arrival 15:05

CC: snakebite to left lower leg.

HPI: 33-year-old man visiting the area on a hiking trip who was struck on the inside of the left ankle on a wooded trail around 13:00, about two hours before arrival. He only glimpsed the snake; it was dull-colored, not banded or bright. Friends drove him in. Pain at the site, no numbness elsewhere, no metallic taste. No trouble breathing, no vision changes, no nausea, vomiting or abdominal pain.

PMH: hypertension, CKD, polycystic kidney disease. Meds: lisinopril. Allergies: NKDA. Social: accountant (formerly a graduate student); never smoker; used to drink socially, stopped after his kidney diagnosis.

Exam: Vitals stable, afebrile. Alert, comfortable. Left leg: two small puncture marks over the medial malleolus, minimal erythema around them, no blistering or necrosis. Swelling limited to the ankle on arrival; marked with pen and timed. Distal pulses intact, sensation normal. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs on arrival: WBC 7.5, Hgb 14.2, platelets 250, PT 12 s, PTT 30 s, fibrinogen 400 mg/dL.

Course: Placed in observation with leg elevated, circumference and swelling margin checked every hour. Around 21:00, roughly eight hours from the bite, he reported more pain and the swelling margin had moved up the leg. Repeat labs at 21:10: WBC 8.2, Hgb 13.8, platelets 195, PT 14 s, PTT 32 s, fibrinogen 300 mg/dL. Discussed with poison center. Continued observation with serial wound and lab checks; no antivenom given. Overnight the swelling stopped advancing, and morning labs showed no further change from the evening set.

Impression: Crotaline (pit viper) envenomation, left lower extremity.

Disposition: discharged 08/09/2025 at 13:30, see discharge instructions. Tetanus is current (Tdap 2023). Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ED Discharge Instructions
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Diagnosis: snakebite (pit viper), left leg.
- Keep the leg raised when resting.
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain (no more than 3000 mg a day). Do NOT take ibuprofen, naproxen or aspirin.
- Keep the wounds clean and dry.
- See your primary doctor in 2-3 days for repeat blood counts and clotting tests.
- Return or call 911 for bleeding gums or nose, blood in urine or stool, spreading swelling, fainting or trouble breathing.

documents.title: Snake bite on vacation
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Heads up, I got bitten by a snake on a hike down in North Carolina yesterday. ER kept me overnight to watch my bloodwork, didn't need the antivenom. Leg is swollen and sore. They want me to see you in 2 to 3 days for blood tests. I'm driving back Monday. Can I come Tuesday? I'll bring the paperwork.

documents.title: RE: Snake bite on vacation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry to hear that! Booked you Tuesday 8/12 at 10:20. Keep the leg up on the drive breaks. If you notice bleeding from gums or nose, blood in your urine, or the swelling climbing, go to the closest ER on the way.

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED/obs stay in NC for a pit viper bite to the L medial ankle on 8/8 (records reviewed, ED note and labs in chart). No antivenom; fibrinogen and platelets dipped on the 8-hour recheck, then held. Since discharge: pain slowly easing, using acetaminophen 1-2x/day, no NSAIDs. No bleeding from gums or nose, urine normal color, no bruising.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. L ankle and lower calf mildly swollen, soft, swelling well below the pen mark from the ED. Two healing puncture marks, scabbed, no drainage, no blistering or discoloration. Calf soft. DP/PT pulses 2+. Moves ankle fully.

A/P: Crotaline envenomation, improving. CBC, PT, fibrinogen today per ED instructions. Elevate, compression sleeve if comfortable, continue acetaminophen only. BP per flowsheet; continue lisinopril. Message if swelling is not gone in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Blood counts and clotting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Platelets are back up to 231, clotting time (PT) 12.4 and fibrinogen 335, all normal. Your blood is clotting normally again, so no more blood tests needed for the bite. Keep the leg up when you can.

documents.title: Leg update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Swelling's all gone, the two marks are just little dots now. Back to walking normally. Also I rebooked my physical for September 23.

documents.title: RE: Leg update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear. See you on the 23rd.

social.value: Former social drinker; none since November 2024

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 33M.

Interval: ADPKD diagnosed 12/2024, CKD stage 1, nephrology following (last 6/2025, stable). HTN on lisinopril 10, home readings low-to-mid 130s/80s. MRA 1/2025 negative for aneurysm. Pit viper bite L ankle 8/8 in NC, observed, no antivenom; swelling gone, no residual symptoms.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: accountant, lives alone. Not drinking since last fall, never smoked. Hiking again, cautiously.
FH: father ADPKD, paternal uncle ruptured cerebral aneurysm, mother HTN.
ROS: negative. No headaches. No flank pain, no hematuria.

Exam: BP 132/84, rest per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, bilateral flank fullness (known enlarged kidneys), nontender. L ankle: two faint healed punctures, no swelling. Skin otherwise clear. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: lipids, CMP. PHQ-2 0. Flu vaccine today. COVID booster at pharmacy when the new one is out.
2. HTN: stable, continue lisinopril 10.
3. ADPKD / CKD 1: nephrology in December.
4. Snakebite: resolved, closing on problem list.
Return 1 year.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group, visit 12/09/2025.

One year since ADPKD diagnosis. Feels well. Had a pit viper bite on a trip in August, observed without antivenom, recovered fully; labs at the time showed transient coagulation changes that normalized. No flank pain or hematuria.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
BP 132/82.
Labs 12/02: creatinine normal, potassium and sodium normal.

Assessment: ADPKD, CKD stage 1, stable. Hypertension on lisinopril.
Plan: no changes. Return in 6 months with BMP and urine albumin/creatinine.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Indication: hemoptysis. Heart size normal. Patchy airspace opacities in both lungs. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: ICU Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medical ICU
Nephrology consultation, 04/01/2026
Requested by: ICU team, for hemoptysis with abnormal urine.

HPI: 34-year-old man with ADPKD, CKD stage 1 and hypertension, known to our outpatient group, who was seen originally for headaches and high blood pressure and last summer for a pit viper bite on the leg. He has noticed dark urine for about a week and began coughing up blood two days ago. No fever, chest pain or recent infection.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD; paternal uncle ruptured cerebral aneurysm; mother HTN.
Social: accountant. Never smoker. Former social drinker, none in over a year.

Exam: T 36.8 C, BP 142/88, HR 80, RR 16, SpO2 92% on room air, now on 2 L nasal cannula. Speaking full sentences. Crackles scattered through both lung fields. Heart regular. Abdomen with large palpable kidneys bilaterally, nontender. No edema, no rash.

Data: creatinine 2.4 (normal at our office in December), BUN 38. Hemoglobin 11.6. UA: large blood, protein 1+, many RBCs with dysmorphic forms on microscopy. Chest film: patchy bilateral infiltrates.

Assessment: pulmonary-renal syndrome; leading concern anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome), with ANCA vasculitis the main alternative.

Recommendations:
- Send anti-GBM antibody, MPO and PR3 ANCA.
- Do not wait for serology: methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily x3 starting today.
- Temporary right internal jugular catheter and daily plasma exchange to begin today.
- Hold lisinopril.
- Kidney biopsy would usually be done, but with enlarged polycystic kidneys the bleeding risk is high; we will rely on serology if strongly positive.
- We will follow daily.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital
Admitted 04/01/2026 (ICU 04/01-04/05, then medical floor). Discharged 04/16/2026.

Principal diagnosis: anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (Goodpasture syndrome) with alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis.
Other: ADPKD, hypertension.

Course: Presented with a week of dark urine and two days of hemoptysis; SpO2 92% on room air, crackles bilaterally, patchy bilateral infiltrates on chest film, creatinine 2.4, active urinary sediment. Admitted to the ICU. Anti-GBM antibody returned at 186 U/mL (reference <20); MPO and PR3 ANCA negative. Biopsy deferred given polycystic kidneys; diagnosis made on serology with the clinical picture.

Treatment: methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily x3, then prednisone 60 mg daily. Plasma exchange daily via a right IJ temporary catheter, 14 sessions in total; catheter removed 04/15 without complication. Oral cyclophosphamide 100 mg daily started (dose reduced for kidney function), planned for 3 months. PJP prophylaxis and a PPI added. Lisinopril held.

Respiratory: 2 L nasal cannula days 1-3, hemoptysis stopped by day 3, weaned to room air and transferred out of the ICU on day 4.
Renal: creatinine peaked at 2.7 on day 3 and improved to 1.9 at discharge. Urine output stayed adequate; no dialysis needed.
Heme: hemoglobin 11.6 on arrival, 10.9 at discharge; no transfusion.
Anti-GBM antibody 34 U/mL on 04/15.

Discharge medications:
- prednisone 60 mg by mouth daily (3 x 20 mg)
- cyclophosphamide 100 mg by mouth daily, morning, with plenty of fluids
- sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 400/80 mg one tablet daily
- pantoprazole 40 mg daily
- HOLD lisinopril until nephrology review
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Nephrology clinic in 3 weeks. Weekly-to-biweekly CBC and BMP while on cyclophosphamide (standing order sent to PCP's lab). Avoid live vaccines. Return for any hemoptysis, fever, or decreased urine.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 05/07/2026.

First clinic visit after admission for anti-GBM disease. Feels steadily better; energy returning. No hemoptysis. Urine clear. Tolerating cyclophosphamide, drinking plenty. Steroid side effects: appetite, restless sleep.

Meds: prednisone 60 mg, cyclophosphamide 100 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, pantoprazole 40 mg. Lisinopril on hold. NKDA.

Labs 05/05 (drawn at an outside lab): creatinine 1.6; anti-GBM 28 U/mL; CBC with normal WBC and platelets.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease responding; antibody nearly cleared, kidney function improving. ADPKD.
Plan:
- Reduce prednisone to 40 mg daily.
- Continue cyclophosphamide 100 mg (3-month course ends early July), TMP-SMX, pantoprazole.
- Labs every 2 weeks as ordered.
- Chest x-ray, 2 views, to document clearing.
- Return in 4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison: portable chest 04/01/2026. The previously seen patchy opacities in both lungs have cleared. Lungs are clear. Heart size and mediastinum normal. No effusion or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of prior bilateral infiltrates. Clear lungs.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 06/04/2026.

Doing well, back to work part-time from home. No respiratory symptoms. Chest x-ray 05/13 clear.

Labs 06/02: anti-GBM 8 U/mL (negative); creatinine 1.5; hemoglobin 13.4; WBC and platelets normal; urine albumin/creatinine 240 mg/g.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease in serologic remission. Residual albuminuria after glomerular injury, superimposed on ADPKD.
Plan:
- Prednisone down to 20 mg daily.
- Restart lisinopril 10 mg daily for albuminuria and blood pressure; BMP in 2 weeks with the standing labs.
- Finish cyclophosphamide early July as planned.
- Continue TMP-SMX and pantoprazole.
- Return in 4 weeks.
NKDA.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 07/02/2026.

Three months from presentation. Asymptomatic. Back to full-time work.

Labs 06/30: creatinine 1.4; potassium normal on lisinopril; WBC and platelets normal throughout the course.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease in remission after plasma exchange, steroids and 3 months of oral cyclophosphamide.
Plan:
- Stop cyclophosphamide today; course complete.
- Prednisone 20 mg for now, plan to reduce next visit.
- Continue TMP-SMX while on 20 mg, pantoprazole, lisinopril 10 mg.
- Labs early August (CBC, BMP, UA, urine albumin/creatinine, anti-GBM), visit after.
NKDA.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 08/06/2026.

Feels well. Lifting again. No hemoptysis, no gross hematuria.

Meds: prednisone 20 mg, TMP-SMX SS, pantoprazole 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg. Cyclophosphamide completed 07/02. NKDA.

Labs 08/04: creatinine 1.4 (eGFR in the 60s), stable for 5 weeks; UA trace blood; urine albumin/creatinine 150 mg/g, down from 240; anti-GBM negative.

Assessment:
1. Anti-GBM disease, sustained serologic remission. Relapse is uncommon.
2. CKD now stage 2 (new baseline creatinine 1.4) with albuminuria, on a background of ADPKD.
3. Hypertension, controlled on lisinopril.
Plan:
- Prednisone to 10 mg daily.
- Stop TMP-SMX.
- Continue pantoprazole while on prednisone.
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg.
- Labs and visit in 6 weeks.
